name: Your Room, Infinity
_why: The plot calls it 'your Victorian bedroom (giant mirror = menu/screen)'. The Lounge is EAST of it, so its one ordinary way out is a door in the RIGHT-hand wall — the map in story.js decides that, not the generator. Regenerated because the bed and mirror were drawn at a tilted 3/4 product-shot angle, foot-to-headboard running diagonally across the frame, instead of this game's flat top-down camera — the only room where that happened, and it broke the sleep interaction: the bed's open foot end (where a character climbs in) did not face the viewer at all.
summary: An opulent VICTORIAN bedroom inside a magical realm — rich, strange and enchanted, not a rustic cottage room. The back wall runs flat and straight across the top of the frame, seen face-on: deep indigo damask wallpaper with gold filigree above dark carved timber wainscot, one continuous moulded picture rail between them at the same height all the way across, and brass sconces burning small violet flames.
_wall_why: A floor-plate room ships ONLY its floor, so the room's own back wall is a PROP and has to be generated like one. Leaving it out of the spec is how a room ends up with one piece of wall art repeated across the whole back.
wall: a wide upright rectangular slab of deep indigo damask wallpaper with gold filigree above dark carved timber wainscot, a moulded picture rail between them, one brass sconce burning a small violet flame, and NO door and NO opening
floor: dark polished PARQUET flooring, small hardwood blocks laid in a herringbone pattern, deep reddish-brown walnut with a waxed sheen, fine grain and subtle wear
camera: TOP-DOWN, exactly like every other room and every other prop in this game — NOT a 3/4 isometric product-shot angle, NOT a diagonal furniture-catalogue view. The bed and the mirror are drawn from directly above and slightly in front, the SAME angle as the back wall and the floor, so they read as objects standing in a top-down room rather than pasted-in concept art.

doors.look: ONE open doorway framed by a carved dark-wood architrave with a moulded pediment — not stone, not a castle arch — with a warmly lit passage receding through it over a patterned runner on dark parquet

contains: an ENORMOUS floor-to-ceiling MIRROR in a heavy carved gilt frame, far taller than a person, its glass filled with a SWIRLING VIOLET-LIGHTNING ENERGY like a portal — NOT a plain reflective surface, NOT a flat tinted pane, NOT a simple diagonal shine streak — standing flat against the back wall and facing SQUARE-ON toward the viewer — not turned to a side angle — on the left. PROPORTIONS, measured off this room's own reference scene: the frame's overall WIDTH is about HALF its HEIGHT — a 1:2 width-to-height rectangle. That is noticeably WIDE for a mirror — NOT a narrow sliver or a slim cheval glass a third as wide as it is tall.
a marble-topped VICTORIAN NIGHTSTAND with a lit three-branch brass candelabra on it

an ORNATE FOUR-POSTER BED with carved dark-wood posts and a deep purple velvet canopy, drawn TOP-DOWN and SQUARE TO THE ROOM like the wall behind it: the headboard flush against the back wall at the TOP of the bed, the FOOT of the bed — open, no headboard, the end a person climbs in from — at the BOTTOM of the bed nearest the viewer. NOT drawn on the diagonal, NOT viewed from a 3/4 corner angle. PROPORTIONS, measured off this room's own reference scene: the bed's total WIDTH, POST TO POST, is nearly as wide as it is tall — close to a SQUARE footprint, about 4:5 width-to-height. This is a SUBSTANTIAL, WIDE four-poster, its posts spread FAR APART — NOT a narrow single bed or cot half as wide as it is tall.

a brass-bound wooden CHEST at the bed's foot: a low, wide, FLAT-TOPPED rectangular box with a FLAT lid — NOT domed, NOT rounded, NOT barrel-shaped or cylindrical — banded with horizontal brass strips and a brass clasp on its front face. Drawn TOP-DOWN and SQUARE TO THE ROOM like the bed beside it, its long side facing the viewer, sitting flush on the floor — NOT tilted, NOT turned to an angle — as its own separate object with its own base. PROPORTIONS, measured off this room's own reference scene: the chest's WIDTH is AT LEAST TWICE its HEIGHT — a 2:1 width-to-height rectangle, LOW and LONG. NOT a tall boxy trunk that is nearly as wide as it is tall — that shape has already been generated once and rejected for reading as a barrel, not a chest.
a patterned crimson and indigo ORIENTAL RUG lying flat on the parquet
a low carved wooden BALUSTRADE running the full width along the near edge, unbroken, with no gap
_measured_why: Read off room.py grid's labelled pixel overlay against bedroom_scene.png, by hand — automated matching between a scene and its independently-generated props was tried (pixel/gradient correlation, ORB feature matching + RANSAC) and does not work, see docs/ROOM_ART_STANDARD.md §5. room.py sizecheck holds story.js to these forever after; re-measure with room.py grid if the scene or the prop art changes and update both together.
